body.en: By default the relay listens on 127.0.0.1 only. No public port is opened unless you change the bind address, and the target server still sees an ordinary Minecraft client.
Handshakes from clients that support wss:// or ws:// are recognised and answered; vanilla Java clients pass through unchanged.
A self-signed certificate is created on first run and can be installed into the Windows trust store with one click.

Offline accounts need no sign-in. Microsoft sign-in uses the device-code flow with a built-in public client ID. A compatible third-party account service can be added with the API root from its provider.
The relay parses the Minecraft protocol, rewrites what a browser cannot send, and keeps the session compatible with Forge, NeoForge and Fabric.
A loopback-only browser control panel for settings, logs, accounts and certificates. The desktop window is the same UI in a native webview.

The /mcp endpoint speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP and exposes 39 tools, resources and prompts for AI clients -- status, config (including appearance and path routes), service control, logs, accounts, certificates, updates, auth, and UI preferences.
Every status query goes to the target server; there is no cached MOTD.
Optionally treat the request path as the target server: /mc244.com -> mc244.com, /hypixel.net -> hypixel.net, /127.0.0.1:25565 -> 127.0.0.1:25565. Mutually exclusive with the path-route table.
